question: A litre of petrol holds about 10 kWh. A fit cyclist pedals out 100 watts. How many hours to match one litre?
move: Price any fuel in hours of human work before calling it cheap.
ask: Which machine in my day does work I could never do by hand, and do I ever notice it?
trap: Guessing an hour or two, because a litre looks so small.
hint: Turn kilowatt-hours into watt-hours, then divide by the cyclist's watts.
steps: One litre of petrol: about 10 kWh = 10,000 watt-hours.
The cyclist delivers 100 watt-hours in each hour.
source: MacKay, Sustainable Energy Without the Hot Air
reference: MacKay, Sustainable Energy – Without the Hot Air, UIT Cambridge, 2009
